trust_decision.summary: The entry name read out of the archive header of a PRX/STX stream is untrusted and must be resolved to a path inside the extraction temp directory before any file is created or decompressed; the decision is taken per extracted entry in the two readers' extractFile methods and centralised in FileHelper.validateTargetFileIsInParentDirectory.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the Primavera P3 PRX reader first; this is the line where the 13-byte NUL-terminated name taken straight from the entry header becomes a File that is then created (line 106) or decompressed into (line 110).

fix_sites.entry_point: org.mpxj.common.FileHelper.validateTargetFileIsInParentDirectory (new public static helper, called from both readers and from the zip extractor)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared helper in org.mpxj.common (looks out of scope for a Primavera advisory)
shared helper - pre-existing zip-slip guard refactored onto the new FileHelper method (behaviour unchanged)
reader (second implementation of the same extraction mechanism, different package and different header layout)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and its reproducer concern a P3 PRX file, so the SureTrak STX reader in another package can be called a separate, older, less-used format that the advisory did not really cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Extraction must keep working for legitimate names: zip entries legitimately use nested sub-directory names and directory entries that are created with mkdirsQuietly (InputStreamHelper.java:200-204), and PRX/STX entries must keep their names verbatim in the flat temp directory because the downstream database readers identify projects purely by filename suffix ('STR.P3' at P3DatabaseReader.java:105, '.DIR' at SureTrakDatabaseReader.java:112). A fix that rejects names containing separators, or that rewrites/strips names to a basename, breaks reading zipped schedules and real P3/SureTrak databases.

O6_input_shapes: NUL-terminated 13-byte file name field in a PRX entry header (P3PRXFileReader.java:96-102)
NUL-terminated 260-byte file name field in an STX entry header (SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:83-90)
entry with dataSize == 0, i.e. empty-file creation branch (P3PRXFileReader.java:104-107; SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:91-94)
entry with dataSize > 0, i.e. PKWARE/Blast-decompressed payload written through an OutputStream (P3PRXFileReader.java:108-115; SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:95-102)
relative traversal names ('../', nested 'a/../../x') as well as names that legitimately stay inside the directory
zip entry names with nested sub-directories and directory entries, through the shared helper (InputStreamHelper.java:192-204)

O7_producer.where: src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/p3/P3PRXFileReader.java:94-102 and src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/suretrak/SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:81-90 (the 13/260-byte name is decoded by getString in the same method that consumes it)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third branch/field inside the same entry loop that names a file to create or decompress (e.g. a long-name or sub-archive field handled after dataSize).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The PRX reader is a self-extracting archive parser whose entries already take two different write branches (empty file vs decompressed payload); a maintainer adding support for another PRX variant would naturally add one more name-to-file branch right here, and it would be easy to validate only the first field.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second archive-expansion helper next to writeZipStreamToTempDir (e.g. writeTarStreamToTempDir / writeGzipStreamToTempDir) that builds Files from entry names.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already treats archive expansion as a shared common-layer concern with one guard; supporting another container format is a routine addition, and a new helper is the obvious place for it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another container/unwrapper fingerprint route (like the DOS self-extracting EXE path at UniversalProjectReader.java:924-963) that hands an archive stream to a reader which writes extracted entries.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: UniversalProjectReader dispatches about twenty formats by fingerprint and already has a self-extracting-EXE wrapper; a new fingerprint wrapper is the project's standard idiom and would be easy to write without the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third sister format reader copied from the STX/PRX pair (a PRX3 or legacy SureTrak variant) with its own fixed-width name field.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two readers are near-verbatim copies of each other, so a third copy is the path of least resistance for a maintainer adding format support, and copying before the guard existed reproduces the flaw.

O9_family: path_traversal (CWE-22, archive-entry path traversal / Zip Slip)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven; maven-compiler-plugin with source/target 1.8 (pom.xml:304-312), surefire 2.22.2; dependencies POI, sqlite-jdbc, jackcess, jsoup, jackson, jaxb, jgoodies-binding, rtfparserkit
O10_build.project_tests: No tests exist for P3 PRX, SureTrak STX, the zip extractor or FileHelper at the pinned commit (no match for P3PRX/SureTrak/STX/validateTargetFile under src/test). The suite under src/test/java/org/mpxj/junit needs an external data directory (-Dmpxj.junit.datadir, MpxjTestData.java:40-59), so the only available checks are new behavioural tests written for the task.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a 'name contains ..' string check (or strip to the basename) only in P3PRXFileReader.extractFile, the reader the report demonstrates, leaving SureTrakSTXFileReader, the dataSize==0 branch and the shared helper inconsistent.
